quests.instruction: When is an important time to wash your hands with soap and water?
quests.correctAnswer: Before you eat or help cook 🧼
options: Only on special days 🎉
Only after you finish dinner 🍽️
Before you eat or help cook 🧼
quests.hint: Germs are too small to see.
quests.explanation: Washing before you eat or cook helps keep germs off your food and out of your mouth.
quests.funFact: Soap helps lift germs off your skin so that water can rinse them away.

quests.instruction: About how long should you scrub your hands with soap?
quests.correctAnswer: About 20 seconds ⏱️
options: About 20 seconds ⏱️
Until the soap is gone 🧴
About 2 seconds ⚡
quests.hint: Think of singing a short song twice.
quests.explanation: Twenty seconds gives the soap enough time to lift germs. A couple of seconds is too quick to do the job.
quests.funFact: Singing Happy Birthday twice takes about twenty seconds.

quests.instruction: Which parts of your hands need washing?
quests.correctAnswer: Backs, fingers and under the nails 🧼
options: Only the very tips of the fingers ☝️
Backs, fingers and under the nails 🧼
Only the palms and nothing else 🖐️
quests.hint: Germs hide in small spaces.
quests.explanation: Germs can hide on the backs of the hands, between the fingers and under the nails, so every part needs washing.
quests.funFact: Fingernails can hold dirt and germs, which is why washing under them matters.

quests.instruction: A cook with long hair ties it back before preparing food. Why?
quests.correctAnswer: So hair does not fall into the food 💇
options: So hair does not fall into the food 💇
So the hair stays dry while stirring 💧
So the cook can see the recipe better 📖
quests.hint: Ask yourself what could land in a bowl.
quests.explanation: Tying hair back keeps it out of the food. It also stops the cook from touching hair and then the food.
quests.funFact: Many restaurant cooks wear hats or hairnets for the same reason.

quests.instruction: You taste soup with a spoon while cooking. What should you do before tasting again?
quests.correctAnswer: Use a clean spoon 🥄
options: Wipe it on your sleeve 👕
Lick the same spoon again 👅
Use a clean spoon 🥄
quests.hint: Germs from your mouth should not go back in the pot.
quests.explanation: A used spoon carries germs from your mouth. A fresh, clean spoon keeps the soup clean.
quests.funFact: Many cooks keep a small cup of clean spoons nearby for tasting.

quests.instruction: You feel a sneeze coming while you help in the kitchen. What is the best thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Turn away and sneeze into your elbow 💪
options: Sneeze into your hands and keep stirring ✋
Turn away and sneeze into your elbow 💪
Sneeze above the open mixing bowl 🥣
quests.hint: Keep the germs away from the food.
quests.explanation: Sneezing into your elbow keeps germs off the food and your hands. Afterward, wash your hands.
quests.funFact: A sneeze can spray tiny droplets quite far, which is why covering it helps.

quests.instruction: Why do we rinse fruits and vegetables under running water before eating them?
quests.correctAnswer: To wash off dirt and germs 💧
options: To make them taste sweeter 🍬
To make them stay fresh for weeks 📆
To wash off dirt and germs 💧
quests.hint: They grew outdoors and were handled before they reached you.
quests.explanation: Rinsing removes dirt and some germs from the skin of fresh produce.
quests.funFact: Even fruits you peel, like melons, should be washed first, because a knife can carry germs from the skin to the inside.

quests.instruction: Which job helps keep the kitchen counter ready for preparing food?
quests.correctAnswer: Washing it with soapy water 🧽
options: Covering it with a towel 🧺
Washing it with soapy water 🧽
Sprinkling flour on top 🌾
quests.hint: Think of cleaning up before you start.
quests.explanation: Soapy water cleans away crumbs and germs. Flour and a towel do not clean the counter.
quests.funFact: Cooks wipe surfaces again after each job, especially after handling raw meat.

quests.instruction: What should you use to dry your hands after washing them in the kitchen?
quests.correctAnswer: A clean, dry towel 🧻
options: A clean, dry towel 🧻
The apron you wore yesterday 👕
Your pants 👖
quests.hint: It should be fresh and not used for anything else.
quests.explanation: A clean, dry towel keeps hands clean. Old aprons and clothes can carry germs and food bits.
quests.funFact: Damp hands pick up germs more easily than dry hands.

quests.instruction: A cook cuts raw chicken on a board. What should happen before the same board is used to cut salad vegetables?
quests.correctAnswer: Wash it with hot soapy water 🧽
options: Wipe it with a dry paper towel 🧻
Wash it with hot soapy water 🧽
Turn it over and use the other side 🔄
quests.hint: Raw chicken can leave germs behind.
quests.explanation: Hot soapy water washes away the germs that raw chicken leaves on a board. A dry wipe or flipping the board does not.
quests.funFact: Keeping raw foods apart from foods eaten without cooking is called preventing cross-contamination.

quests.instruction: Where is the safest place in the fridge to keep raw meat?
quests.correctAnswer: In a covered container on the bottom shelf 🧊
options: In a covered container on the bottom shelf 🧊
Open on the top shelf, above the fresh fruit 🧊
On the door shelf, right next to the butter 🚪
quests.hint: Ask yourself where drips could fall.
quests.explanation: Raw meat juices can drip. Kept low and covered, they cannot land on foods that are eaten raw.
quests.funFact: Fridges usually keep ready-to-eat foods higher up and raw meat at the bottom.

quests.instruction: Why should cooked meat go on a clean plate, not the plate that held it raw?
quests.correctAnswer: Germs from the raw meat could spread to it 🦠
options: The plate would make the meat too cold ❄️
Cooked meat would lose all its flavor 😋
Germs from the raw meat could spread to it 🦠
quests.hint: Ask yourself what was on the plate before.
quests.explanation: Germs from the raw meat can stay on the plate and spread to cooked meat. A clean plate prevents that.
quests.funFact: Heat kills germs in cooked meat, so the danger comes from germs left on the old plate.

quests.instruction: Which job is a safe way for a child to help with cooking?
quests.correctAnswer: Washing vegetables at the sink 🥕
options: Washing vegetables at the sink 🥕
Using the big sharp knife 🔪
Lifting a pot of boiling water ♨️
quests.hint: No sharp tools or heat are needed.
quests.explanation: Washing vegetables is safe and helpful. Sharp knives and boiling water need a grown-up.
quests.funFact: Many children's cookbooks start with easy jobs like washing, mixing and measuring.

quests.instruction: Why do cooks turn pot handles away from the front edge of the stove?
quests.correctAnswer: So nobody bumps the pot and knocks it over 🍳
options: So the pot cooks faster on the front burner 🔥
So nobody bumps the pot and knocks it over 🍳
So all the pots line up neatly in a row 📐
quests.hint: Think about arms and elbows passing by.
quests.explanation: A handle that sticks out can be knocked, and a hot pot could spill. Turning it inward keeps everyone safe.
quests.funFact: Handles also stay cooler when they are not sitting over the flames.

quests.instruction: Some water spills on the kitchen floor. What is the best thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Tell a grown-up and wipe it up 🧽
options: Leave it there and clean up later 🕒
Step around it every time you pass 🚶
Tell a grown-up and wipe it up 🧽
quests.hint: Wet floors are slippery.
quests.explanation: Wiping up a spill quickly, with a grown-up's help, stops anyone from slipping.
quests.funFact: Slips are a common kitchen accident, so cooks clean up spills straight away.

quests.instruction: A classmate is allergic to eggs. What is the safest choice when you want to share a snack?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask a grown-up or the classmate first 🙋
options: Hide what is in the snack 🤫
Ask a grown-up or the classmate first 🙋
Share it anyway because it is small 🤏
quests.hint: Allergic reactions can be serious.
quests.explanation: Even a small amount of a food can make an allergic person ill, so always check first.
quests.funFact: Many schools have rules about sharing food to keep students with allergies safe.

quests.instruction: Why do food packages list ingredients such as milk, eggs and peanuts?
quests.correctAnswer: To warn people who are allergic 🏷️
options: To make the label look longer 📏
To show which foods taste best 😋
To warn people who are allergic 🏷️
quests.hint: Some people must avoid certain foods completely.
quests.explanation: Labels name common allergens so that people with allergies can avoid them.
quests.funFact: Common food allergens include milk, eggs, peanuts, tree nuts, fish, shellfish, wheat, soy and sesame.

quests.instruction: A cracker drops on the kitchen floor. What is the safest thing to do?
quests.correctAnswer: Throw it away 🗑️
options: Throw it away 🗑️
Wait five seconds and eat it ⏱️
Brush it off and eat it 🧹
quests.hint: Think about everything that has walked across a floor.
quests.explanation: Floors can carry germs and dirt, and food picks them up right away. It is safest to throw the cracker away.
quests.funFact: Germs can reach food the moment it touches a dirty surface, so there is no safe waiting time.

quests.instruction: Which list shows the best order for getting ready to cook?
quests.correctAnswer: Wash hands, wipe the counter, gather ingredients 🧼
options: Wipe the counter, gather ingredients, wash hands 🧼
Gather ingredients, wipe the counter, wash hands 🧼
Wash hands, wipe the counter, gather ingredients 🧼
quests.hint: Clean hands touch everything else.
quests.explanation: Hands go first, because they touch the counter and the ingredients. Wiping the counter comes before the food goes on it.
quests.funFact: Chefs call getting everything ready before cooking mise en place, a French phrase.

quests.instruction: Why should people not eat raw cookie dough made with raw eggs and raw flour?
quests.correctAnswer: Raw eggs and raw flour can carry germs 🥚
options: Raw eggs and raw flour can carry germs 🥚
It would be much too hard to chew 🍪
It would taste far too sweet to enjoy 🍬
quests.hint: Ask yourself what is raw in the bowl.
quests.explanation: Baking kills the germs that raw eggs and flour can carry, so dough should be baked before it is eaten.
quests.funFact: Flour comes from a field crop, so it is a raw ingredient that needs cooking, just like eggs.

quests.instruction: Why is chicken cooked all the way through before it is eaten?
quests.correctAnswer: Heat kills germs that raw chicken can carry 🔥
options: Cooking makes chicken grow bigger and wider 📈
Heat kills germs that raw chicken can carry 🔥
Cold makes the chicken taste better ❄️
quests.hint: Think about what raw meat can carry.
quests.explanation: Cooking until the meat is hot all the way through kills germs, so the chicken is safe to eat.
quests.funFact: Cooks use a food thermometer to check that meat is hot enough in the middle.

quests.instruction: Which water is the safest to drink?
quests.correctAnswer: Clean tap water or bottled water 💧
options: Clean tap water or bottled water 💧
Water scooped from a nearby pond 🐟
Water from a muddy puddle outside 🟤
quests.hint: Look for water that has been cleaned.
quests.explanation: Clean tap water or bottled water is made safe to drink. Puddles and ponds can hold germs.
quests.funFact: Water treatment plants clean water so that it is safe to drink in many places.

quests.instruction: Why should friends not share the same cup or straw?
quests.correctAnswer: Germs can pass from mouth to mouth 🦠
options: The cup would get too hot to hold 🔥
The drink would run out much faster 🥤
Germs can pass from mouth to mouth 🦠
quests.hint: Ask yourself where a straw has been.
quests.explanation: Germs can pass from one person's mouth to another's on a shared cup or straw.
quests.funFact: Colds and other illnesses can spread when people share cups, forks and straws.

quests.instruction: Why is milk heated, or pasteurized, before it is sold?
quests.correctAnswer: Heating kills harmful germs 🔥
options: Heating makes it thicker and creamier 🥛
Heating kills harmful germs 🔥
Heating makes it taste much sweeter 🍬
quests.hint: Think about germs.
quests.explanation: Pasteurizing milk heats it briefly to kill harmful germs, and the milk stays fresh for longer.
quests.funFact: Pasteurization is named after Louis Pasteur, a French scientist from the 1800s.

quests.instruction: Which is a safe habit when you eat?
quests.correctAnswer: Sit down while you eat 🪑
options: Eat while lying down 🛏️
Run around with food in your mouth 🏃
Sit down while you eat 🪑
quests.hint: Think about what helps food go down safely.
quests.explanation: Sitting up and chewing well helps food go down safely. Running or lying down can make you choke.
quests.funFact: Sitting and chewing well make it easier to swallow safely.

quests.instruction: Whole grapes can block a very young child's throat. What helps make them safer?
quests.correctAnswer: Cutting them into small pieces 🍇
options: Cutting them into small pieces 🍇
Giving them while the child plays 🏃
Freezing them hard 🧊
quests.hint: Smaller pieces slide down more easily.
quests.explanation: Cutting grapes into small pieces lowers the chance of choking. Freezing makes them harder and playing makes choking more likely.
quests.funFact: Round, firm foods like grapes, hot dogs and nuts are common choking hazards for little children.

quests.instruction: Why should you wash your hands after petting a dog or cat, before you eat?
quests.correctAnswer: Pets can carry germs on fur and paws 🐕
options: Pet fur makes food go stale faster ⏳
Pets can carry germs on fur and paws 🐕
Washing keeps the pet's fur clean too 🐾
quests.hint: Ask yourself where animals walk and sleep.
quests.explanation: Animals can carry germs on their fur and paws, and washing keeps those germs from reaching your mouth.
quests.funFact: Farmers and chefs wash their hands often for the same reason, because hands touch so many things.

quests.instruction: Which list shows good kitchen hygiene?
quests.correctAnswer: Wash hands, tie back hair, use clean tools 🧼
options: Wash hands, tie back hair, use clean tools 🧼
Cook fast, skip washing, share one spoon 🥄
Taste with fingers, wipe hands on pants 🧢
quests.hint: Look for the list where everything keeps germs away.
quests.explanation: Clean hands, tied-back hair and clean tools all keep germs out of food. The other lists spread germs.
quests.funFact: Good habits in the kitchen protect everyone who eats the food.

quests.instruction: Which food should be kept apart from raw meat because it will not be cooked before eating?
quests.correctAnswer: Fresh fruit salad 🍓
options: Uncooked rice 🍚
Fresh fruit salad 🍓
Frozen chicken 🍗
quests.hint: Look for something eaten without cooking.
quests.explanation: Fruit salad is eaten as it is, so any germs from raw meat would not be killed. Chicken and rice will be cooked.
quests.funFact: Raw meat and fresh produce are packed in separate bags at the shop for the same reason.

quests.instruction: Which list shows the right order for washing your hands?
quests.correctAnswer: Wet, soap, scrub, rinse, dry 🧼
options: Rinse, scrub, soap, dry, wet 🧼
Soap, dry, rinse, scrub, wet 🧼
Wet, soap, scrub, rinse, dry 🧼
quests.hint: Hands must be wet before the soap goes on.
quests.explanation: Wet your hands, add soap, scrub, rinse the soap away and dry with a clean towel.
quests.funFact: Warm or cold water both work, as long as you scrub with soap for twenty seconds.
